children: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand was non-committal at its September policy meeting about when the next interest rate hike might come but was clearly leaning toward a pause at the next meeting in October, says Matthew Galt, an economist at ANZ. Global developments since then have been suggesting it would be prudent to hike sooner rather than later, and the resilience shown in 2Q GDP data adds further pressure in that direction, he adds. ANZ continues to expect a 25-basis-point hike by the RBNZ in October. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
